note: Planted ground truth. Everything not listed here is ordinary noise. Quantities are the generator's true effects.

scenarios.title: Ink over-consumption on one press
scenarios.truth: Usage rate +12% over standard for one week (dispenser drift; see the P02 calibration event on 2026-11-02).

scenarios.title: Bad substrate lot
scenarios.truth: +5.5 pp spoilage on every run that drew from the lot, across presses (P01, P02, P03, P06); MES reason codes skew to SUB/JAM.

scenarios.title: High-spoilage shift
scenarios.truth: +2.8 pp spoilage on every P03 shift-C run; reason codes skew to REG/WIP.

scenarios.title: Out-of-date usage standard
scenarios.truth: Actual usage fell 14% (process change) but the BOM still carries the old rate, so the variance is favorable and the standard overstates need — a standards problem, not a floor problem.

scenarios.title: Seasonal humidity spoilage
scenarios.truth: Spoilage rises 0.12 pp per RH point above 56% in Hall 2 (mes_environment); peaks Jul–Aug; reason codes SUB/REG.

scenarios.title: Vendor lead-time slip
scenarios.truth: Actual lead time ≈ 77 days vs 42 in the item master; vendor still promises 42. Safety stock has quietly eroded.
scenarios.note: Short = projected book stock below safety stock within the item's lead time, counting open POs only.

scenarios.title: Production-plan increase
scenarios.truth: A plan-driven forecast shows the shortfall; a historical-average forecast does not.

scenarios.title: Hidden over-use of a backflushed material
scenarios.truth: Actual use +9% (recirculation leak). The ERP backflushes at standard, so run-level variance is invisible; it only surfaces as negative cycle-count adjustments.

scenarios.title: Issues posted in the wrong period
scenarios.truth: Issue transactions carry the posting date, not the run date, so September ERP consumption is understated and October overstated vs MES.

scenarios.title: Missing, duplicate and mis-keyed MES records
scenarios.truth: ERP completions reference runs that MES lacks; some runs were keyed twice (ERP completed twice, backflush doubled); two manual entries have transposed printed counts that disagree with the ERP substrate issue.
